Subject: Acceptance criteria for on-prem / VPC escrow, evidence & erase

Irene —

Thanks for taking this. Our security team needs to finalize the acceptance criteria for our on-prem/VPC deployment (CopenHealth) before legal signs off. Two asks: a) what concrete evidence will Redwood provide to demonstrate a successful tenant wipe (for both customer-managed storage and Redwood-hosted artifacts in the control plane), and b) what escrow artifacts are available if we request a snapshot for compliance post-exit?

High level constraints:
- We require chain-of-custody evidence for any handback or assisted wipe.
- Prefer a notary-ready statement or structured artifact (CSV/manifest) listing object IDs, timestamps, and deletion checksums where possible.
- If keys are customer-managed, we need guidance on the interplay with snapshot/escrow retrieval.

Can you share a checklist (technical + legal) and an ETA for delivering that checklist and an initial evidence template? We have a compliance review on 2026-06-02.

Best,
Evan Cole
Head of Infrastructure, CopenHealth

Evan —

Appreciate the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Product Ops) and Dev (Solutions) to capture both the legal/evidence artifacts and the operational mechanics.

Quick answers up front:
1) We can provide a structured evidence bundle post-wipe that includes an object-level manifest, deletion receipts (where storage APIs support it), snapshot manifests, and a signed attestation from Redwood describing the operations performed and timestamps.
2) Escrow: we offer optional encrypted snapshots (customer option) retained for a configurable short window (default 30 days) and can provide an escrow export under strict access controls; when keys are customer-managed, we will not be able to decrypt the snapshot — instead we provide metadata and the wrapped key artifact for your KMS.

Request to you: can you confirm whether you will manage KMS keys (BYOK) or want Redwood KMS for the escrow snapshots? That determines what we can deliver as decrypted evidence.

ETA: Marissa and I will produce a checklist + evidence template by EOD 2026-05-21. If that works, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through items before your compliance review.

Evan / Irene —

Thanks — attaching an evidence template and a first-pass checklist (see attachment: Copen_Evidence_Template_v2.xlsx). High-level acceptance criteria we propose:

Operational acceptance checklist (minimum):
- Confirmation of tenant data object manifest: listing of object IDs and sizes as-of snapshot time (CSV).
- Snapshot manifest: snapshot ID, creation timestamp, region, and replication metadata.
- Deletion operations log: sequence of API calls (request ID, actor, timestamp) showing delete operations and any automatic tombstones.
- KV/Model cache eviction confirmation: record that in-memory caches and persisted KV caches were cleared.
- Key handling record: if BYOK, provide wrapped key metadata and KMS request/rotation logs; if Redwood KMS, provide key destruction proof (HSM KMS logs).
- Control plane artifact purge: list of control plane records removed (tenant metadata, billing tokens).
- Access log extract for the handback window (ISO8601 timestamps).

Evidence integrity:
- SHA256 checksums for manifests (signed and timestamped).
- Signed attestation from Redwood security lead with reference to the specific tenant ID and action set.

Escrow options:
- Short-term encrypted snapshot (30-day default): stored encrypted with either customer key or Redwood-managed key. Retrieval requires signed request + compliance approval.
- Long-term escrow by exception: subject to contract, with notarized attestation and additional fees.

Notes about delivery and notary: we can produce a Redwood-signed attestation. For an independent notary, we recommend adding a clause for a third-party audit at exit (we can coordinate).

I've attached SLA_redline_Copen.pdf with suggested language for deletion SLAs and evidence delivery windows.

Let us know if you need a notarized signature or a certified third-party witness included in the attestation.

—Marissa
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Evan —

Technical clarifications from an implementation perspective:
- If you choose BYOK (customer-managed KMS): we will store snapshots encrypted with your wrapped key. We can provide the wrapped-key metadata (key ID, wrapping algorithm, timestamp). Redwood cannot produce plaintext evidence (we cannot decrypt). To offer a decrypted manifest for your auditors, you would need to unwrap the key in your environment or authorize a one-time decryption flow under a joint SOP.
- For Redwood-managed KMS: we can generate key destruction evidence from our HSM logs (subject to audit redaction rules).
- Proof-of-delete: depending on object store, we provide either a deletion receipt (object-store supported) or a tombstone manifest plus a subsequent verification job that queries object existence after TTL and produces an existence report.
- Control-plane ephemeral caches: we run a deterministic cache purge and provide a cache-eviction event log and a post-purge validation run (hash comparison against a zeroed manifest).

Operational timeline estimate: 5–7 business days from formal handback request to produce the full evidence bundle (if no BYOK decryption required). BYOK flows add coordination (we estimate +3 business days). Notary or third-party witness add at least one additional week for scheduling.

I'll add a short-runbook for the handback window and upload to the secure drive; linking that in the final checklist.

—Dev
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
